title: What If Cash Vanished Completely? Sweden Is Close

scenes.text: What if cash vanished for good? One country is closer than any other, and it is worried.
In Sweden, notes and coins were about one percent of the economy in 2018, versus around ten percent across Europe.
Over 95 percent of purchases in Stockholm are by card, and over half of Swedish bank branches no longer keep cash on site.
Then come the people left behind. About a million Swedes aren't comfortable banking on phones or computers, many of them older.
A power cut or cyberattack could kill every card terminal. Sweden's crisis agency tells households to keep some cash at home.
That's why its central bank is testing a digital krona, so some money stays in the state's hands, not only the banks'.

description:
What if cash vanished for good?
Sweden is closest, with notes and coins at about one percent of its economy, but its crisis agency still tells households to keep some cash.
